newsitem.title: HUNGARY: HUNGARY HAS LITTLE RISK OF CZECH SPILLOVER - ANALYSTS.
newsitem.headline: HUNGARY HAS LITTLE RISK OF CZECH SPILLOVER - ANALYSTS.

text.p: The Hungarian forint faces little risk of a spillover of the Czech crown's weakness because Hungary's exports are strong and its C/A deficit is substantially less, analysts said on Tuesday.
"I think Hungary is quite all right for the timebeing," said Istvan Racz, an economist for CS First Boston in Budapest.

"Hungary's current account problem is substantially less than Czech Republic's and, interestingly, the deficit fell in the first two months (of 1997) due to a high growth rate in merchandise exports."
Hungary's current account deficit was $498 million for January and February 1997, compared to $607 million for the same period last year, according to the national bank.
Exports for the January-February period this year grew to $2.81 billion, compared to $1.98 billion for the same two months last year.
Attila Torok of Postabank Securities agreed the situation in Hungary "is much better" than in Czech Republic.
"There is a continuous inflow of capital and the central bank of Hungary raised its rates for six-month and one-year deposits at the end of March," Torok said.
"The balance of payments of the Hungarian economy is stable and the CPI is also stable," he added.
Torok noted that Hungary had completed a further partial privatisation of state oil conglomerate MOL Rt that was heavily oversubscribed domestically and internationally.
"In the Czech economy there are problems in privatisation," he said. "It was not a real privatisation, and the value of real wages is higher than in Hungary."
Racz said it would be a mistake to lump Hungary together with Czech Republic or with Thailand, another emerging market economy suffering from weakness of its currency.
"The fact that a country (Czech Republic) not so very far away from Hungary is in trouble is no reason Hungary should be in trouble," he said.
"The key thing is that exports are growing very fast in Hungary," he added.
